parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Fig. 5.1 shows two parallel conducting plates that are in a vacuum. The plates are separated by a distance of $6.7\text{ cm}$ and have a potential difference (p.d.) of $430\text{ V}$ between them.

{{figure:figure_5_1.png}}

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw four field lines to represent the electric field between the plates.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the strength $E$ of the electric field between the plates.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
An electron travels at a speed of $2.6 \times 10^7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards the region between the plates, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

On Fig. 5.1, draw the path of the electron as it moves between and beyond the plates.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: A uniform magnetic field is now applied in the region of the electric field in Fig. 5.1, so that the electron in (b)(iii) travels undeviated through the region.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Determine the direction of the uniform magnetic field.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to the forces exerted by the two fields on the electron, why the path of the electron is undeviated.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the flux density $B$ of the uniform magnetic field. Give a unit with your answer.
